sentences.text: The original type specimen was a juvenile individual measuring approximately 4.5 meters in length and weighing about 200 kilograms.
This holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is cataloged as MPEF-PV 1672 and consists of a left tibia bone.
Additional remains referred to the species include vertebrae, teeth, ribs, hip fragments, femurs, a fourth metatarsal, and a foot phalanx.
Condorraptor is considered one of the largest early South American theropods, reaching an estimated length of about 7 meters, though it was initially thought to be only 4 to 5 meters long.
The animal is characterized by a posterior notch between the fibular condyles, the absence of the medial proximal part of the tibia, and a deep lateral fossa on the cnemial crest.
Condorraptor was one of the earliest large theropod dinosaurs found in South America, discovered in Lower Jurassic rocks in Argentina.
The species Condorraptor currumili was first described by scientists in 2005.
The genus name means 'robber from Cerro Condor' and the species name honors Hipolito Currumil, the landowner where the fossils were found.
In 2007, a larger articulated skeleton comprising about 70% of the bones was discovered at Cerro Condor.
The team that found the articulated skeleton included Oliver Rauhut, Magali Cárdenas, Leandro Canessa, Mariano Caffa, José Luis Carballido, and Pablo Puerta.
The cervical vertebrae of Condorraptor feature a pleurocoel located in the anterior portion at the posteroventral angle of the parapophysis.
A large nutrient foramen is present on the lateral side of the ischial peduncle in the ilium of Condorraptor.
The fourth metatarsal of Condorraptor has a distinct step on the dorsal and distal articular surface.

A fragmentary partial skull described in 2007 is possibly attributed to Condorraptor based on its size, locality, and tetanuran characteristics, despite differences from Piatnitzkysaurus cranial material.
Research by Benson in 2010 classified Condorraptor as a piatnitzkysaurid megalosauroid and the closest relative to Piatnitzkysaurus.
Condorraptor is classified within the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
The genus Condorraptor belongs to the parent group Piatnitzkysauridae.
Condorraptor is classified as a reptile.
Condorraptor lived during the Middle Jurassic period, approximately 162 million years ago, in what is now South America.
Condorraptor lived between the Toarcian and Bajocian stages, from 180.4 to 168.6 million years ago.
Due to the fragmentary nature of the initial discovery, the classification of Condorraptor remains incomplete, though it is known to be a basal tetanuran likely related to Piatnitzkysaurus.
